KAVIR

ANALYTIC SCAFFOLD IRAN · 31 PROVINCES v2 · NOV 2026

A subnational socioeconomic-stress heatmap of the Islamic Republic of Iran — every province scored on eight indicators across two axes: structural fragility (poverty, joblessness, human-capital drain, fiscal dependence) and acute 2024–26 shocks (currency & inflation, water/power/environment, conflict & strike, fuel & energy-subsidy). Version 2 adds satellite views — NASA basemaps under the map, 2000–2026 time-lapses of six water-stress sites and a live imagery explorer — and a sourced register of economic triggers of household stress. The Digital Public-Sphere Signals and Communication Channels lenses carry over from v1.

Read this first. This is an analytic scaffold, not a live feed, a forecast, or an operational tool. Scores are relative stress indices (0–100) graded from public statistics (Statistical Center of Iran, Central Bank of Iran, World Bank, IMF, ILO — which tend to understate hardship), reputable secondary analysis, and explicit analyst judgment where per-province data is thin. It measures socioeconomic conditions and the visibility of distress — not the probability of political change, and not any individual, account, or group. The digital layer is a modelled, aggregate read of open platforms, not monitoring or a live crawl. Province scores are unchanged from v1; the trigger register is descriptive — what has caused hardship, how it reaches households, and what to watch — and every 2026 figure in it is tagged by how it was checked.

Satellite views — a look across the country

Three ways to look. The MAP tab now takes a satellite basemap under the province scores (true colour, night lights, vegetation, surface heat, population). Below, six time-lapses follow the water bodies behind the map's highest-loading acute indicator, one frame a year from 2000 to 2026. And the live explorer at the bottom streams current high-resolution and daily imagery for any place and date.

Water-stress time-lapses, 2000–2026

Each frame is the clearest NASA MODIS Terra true-colour scene (250 m) from the same few weeks of every year, so seasons are comparable. Drag the slider or press play. Frames are embedded in this file and work offline.

Live imagery explorer

Pan and zoom the whole country on live tiles, with the province scores as an overlay. Pick high-resolution imagery for detail, or a daily NASA layer and a date to see any day since 2000 — a dust storm, a flood, a lake in a given summer, city lights on a given night.

The explorer loads map tiles from NASA GIBS, Esri and EOX, and the Leaflet map library from cdnjs. Nothing else in this dashboard makes a network request. It needs an internet connection and will not load inside some sandboxed previews — open the HTML file in a browser if it fails.

Reading the layers

Economic triggers of household stress

The province scores describe conditions. This tab describes events: the dated, visible changes — a price decree, a missed payday, a tap that stops — that have turned chronic hardship into acute stress in Iran, where each stands in November 2026, and what to watch. It is a record and a monitoring aid, not a forecast and not a guide to action.

Trigger register

Twelve triggers. For each: what it is, how it reaches households, who is hit first, documented precedents, where it stands now, what has cushioned it, and what to watch. The provincial pointer uses an indicator the map already carries — no new scoring is introduced.

Episode ledger

What changed, and what followed. read = the figure was checked against the source in this build; summary = known from a search summary only; record = pre-2026 history as widely reported.

Seasonal baseline

Several pressures return on the climatic and administrative calendar every year. Knowing the usual timing keeps a seasonal recurrence from being misread as a new shock — and shows when stacked windows coincide. Typical timing only; not a forecast.

How to read this tab

Digital public-sphere signals — reading the open platforms

A second lens on the same 31 provinces: what Iran's open, public social and messaging platforms reveal about economic distress. This is a modelled, aggregate read — not a live crawl, not monitoring of any person or account. Each province's observed signal is its real economic pressure filtered through how openly that pressure can surface — which, under Iran's filtering, VPN dependence and self-censorship, is why the open picture is systematically thinner than the reality beneath it.

Instability typology — structural × acute

Each province placed by structural fragility (horizontal) against acute 2024–26 shock (vertical). Dashed lines are the national medians; the four quadrants sort provinces into distinct problems. Point colour and size scale with the combined score.

Pillar matrix — every province × eight indicators

The full scored grid. Click a column header to sort. Each cell is shaded within its own indicator's national range, so columns are internally comparable. S = structural, A = acute.

Bottom line & key judgments

Indicators & warnings — what to watch

Method

Sources — Admiralty-graded

Reliability graded A–F (source track record) × 1–6 (information credibility), after the NATO Admiralty System. No source here is non-public; nothing below is operational.

2026 economic reporting — opened and read in this build

Figures in the Triggers tab attributed to these were checked against the article text. They are press reports of official Iranian statistics and statements, not the primary releases.

From search summaries — verify before citing
